taxonomic_note: Accepted species. Kew recognizes var. decidua and var. mulleri; the learner remains species-level.
look_here_first: Ask whether the holly is deciduous. Possumhaw drops its leaves and often leaves dense red-orange drupes exposed along pale gray twigs in winter.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — project Hays native-source list plus naturally occurring Purola Preserve material. Travis — Pace Bend Park/native central-Texas documentation. Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center county treatment.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Landscape plantings are not used as county-native evidence.

best_field_traits: alternate simple leaves, elliptic to obovate/spatulate
thin-textured leaves with shallow crenate to crenate-serrate margins
small axillary white flowers; plants primarily dioecious
female plants bear red to orange-red drupes clustered along twigs
fruit commonly persists after leaf drop
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Within local hollies, deciduous winter-bare fruiting twigs are the fastest field separator.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Yaupon is evergreen with much smaller leathery leaves and low crenate teeth. American holly is an evergreen tree with much larger thick leaves bearing stiff spine-tipped teeth.
